text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] runtime-prod: sudden GPU OOMs on serving pool 'rerank-v2' — page created, paging duty paged @devon (oncall-sre) 2425016789

maria (prod-plat): saw a spike of 503s and explicit OOM traces on /v1/generate around 12:03 UTC. Multiple hosts in rerank-v2 returned CUDA OOM. customer-facing error rate ~3.8%.

devon (oncall-sre): I'm taking it. first pass: collecting nvidia-smi + runtime logs from the affected hosts. can someone post the earliest stack traces?

ashok (eng-runtime): adding my hypotheses early: suspect fragmentation + KV cache retention causing address space pressure during large batch bursts. could be long-tail requests that keep KV pages pinned.

maria (prod-plat): timeline so far (rough):
- 12:02:10 UTC — traffic surge from batch job from customer A (bulk rerank)
- 12:03:05 UTC — latency climb, some 500/503s start
- 12:03:40 UTC — first CUDA OOM in host rerank-03
- 12:04:12 UTC — OOMs spread to rerank-01 and -02
- 12:05:00 UTC — started route fallback to smaller model (auto-fallback policy)
- 12:06:20 UTC — applied first mitigation (reduced batch size on canary)

devon (oncall-sre): raw snippet from /var/log/redwood/runtime.log on rerank-03 around failure (truncated):
```
[12:03:40] ERROR runtime: failed to allocate GPU memory: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 104,857,600 bytes.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/serve.py", line 412, in handle_request
    outputs = model.forward(batch)
  File "/opt/models/llm/attention.py", line 88, in forward
    kv_cache.append(kv_page)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```

devon (oncall-sre): nvidia-smi from rerank-03 taken at 12:03:38:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.60.11    Driver Version: 525.60.11    CUDA Version: 12.1   |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-SXM4-40GB  Off        | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                  N/A |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |
|  GPU   PID  Type  Process name                Usage   |
|  0    8841  C    python serve.py               37258MiB |
|  0    8899  C    python collect.py             1024MiB  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Note: shows 37.2GiB in use on 40GiB card but fragmentation observed (free blocks not reusable).

ashok (eng-runtime): quick memory stats from our telemetry (12:03 UTC window):
- avg live_kv_pages_per_gpu: 14,302
- avg contiguous_free_chunks: 1.8 (median)
- page_fault_swap_count: increased x3 compared to baseline
Those contiguous_free_chunks number is low — points at fragmentation.

sre-alex: any evidence of a leaking handle or pinned tensors?

devon (oncall-sre): grep for 'pinned' returns a few long-lived pinned buffers in rerank-03 logs tied to an older batch path (legacy batching fallback). i'll capture heap + GPU allocations and upload.

devon (oncall-sre): mitigation plan applied at 12:06:20 on canary (rerank-04):
- runtime.batch_max_size: 64 -> 32
- kvcache.eviction_policy: aggressive (target_free_chunks=4)
- temporarily disable speculative prefetching for KV pages
We routed 10% of traffic to canary. result: no new OOMs on canary for 6min, error rate on canary fell to baseline.

support-julie: customer impact summary so far: ~7 customer jobs got 5xx during 12:03-12:08. largest impacted is PartnerCorp (3 jobs); ops routed their heavy rerank to dedicated reserve at 12:07 — they reported degraded throughput but no failures. notif sent to PartnerCorp support channel.

maria (prod-plat): good catch on canary. next steps: dominate traffic fallback, and collect detailed allocation traces for an RCA. assign owner for timeline + artifact collection?

devon (oncall-sre): i'll own immediate artifact collection. uploading logs and profiles to gs://redwood-incident-logs/2425016789/. grabbing cuda-memcheck + nvprof traces from rerank-03 now.

ashok (eng-runtime): hypothesis tracker (early):
1) KV cache retention + fragmentation: eviction policy too conservative causing many small free chunks -> OOM on burst.
2) Legacy batching path pinned buffers that prevented compaction (confirmed partial grep).
3) Kernel-level allocation churn during attention recompute exacerbates fragmentation.
We should validate by: a) reproducing with stress tool that mimics PartnerCorp batch pattern, b) checking if compaction routine runs (kvcache.compact) and if it returns success, c) correlating per-request KV page lifetimes.

devon (oncall-sre): reproduction note: can reproduce locally with stress tool using same batch shape and KV page sequence; observed OOM after ~1200 requests within 10 minutes. will upload repro script too.

sre-alex: for immediate P0 fixes we should: 1) keep reduced batch size globally for 30m, 2) enable aggressive kvcache eviction cluster-wide, 3) schedule rolling restart of rerank pool with upgraded runtime that forces kvcache compaction on startup. any downsides?

ashok (eng-runtime): rolling restarts will clear fragmentation but are disruptive; set maintenance window <10min per host, staggered. compaction on startup landed in runtime v1.14 (safe). batch size drop will increase latency/cost but prevent failures.

maria (prod-plat): decision: apply points 1+2 now, plan restarts in 30m while monitoring. opsbot: apply policy change to cluster rerank-v2 (batch_max_size=32, kvcache.eviction=aggressive)

opsbot: acknowledged. applying config to rerank-v2 pool, will report back on completion.

opsbot: config rollout complete to 12 nodes in pool at 12:07:45 UTC.

devon (oncall-sre): post-change metrics (12:08-12:12): 503s down from 3.8% -> 0.6%, no new OOM traces after config rollout.

support-julie: updated customers, PartnerCorp's jobs resubmitted and succeeded on dedicated lane. will follow up with full impact email.

maria (prod-plat): collecting RCA artifacts:
- logs + stack traces: gs://redwood-incident-logs/2425016789/logs.tar.gz
- nvprof/nv-memcheck artifacts: gs://redwood-incident-logs/2425016789/profiles/
- repro script: gs://redwood-incident-logs/2425016789/repro.sh
Please add notes to the incident doc: /incidents/2425016789 (I'll create the formal postmortem after we confirm root cause).

ashok (eng-runtime): quick recommendation for longer term: implement incremental compaction (reduce pinned region lifetimes), add a fragmentation alert on contiguous_free_chunks < 2 threshold, and consider periodic kvcache.swap to DRAM when GPU free contiguous is low.

devon (oncall-sre): handing off for post-incident RCA to ashok and maria. I'll remain on watch for another 30m then sign off. :thumbsup:

maria (prod-plat): thanks everyone. great quick coordination.

incident-bot: incident state -> mitigated. creating follow-up ticket for RCA and planned restarts.
